# How do generative foundation models feed biology to language? A scoping review of input representations in text–biology models

*Draft v0.1, 2026-10-07. Every number is generated by `scripts/build_prisma_flow.py`,
`scripts/build_review_synthesis.py` or the operation library build; do not edit numbers by hand.
`[CITE]` marks a citation still to be added from the included-study table. `[PENDING]` marks
results that depend on the corpus-wide operation decomposition, which has not been run yet.*

## Abstract

**Background.** Generative foundation models increasingly combine natural language with biological
data such as sequences, expression profiles, images and graphs. How biological data are turned into
something a language model can consume is decided per paper and rarely compared across them.

**Objective.** To map which generative text–biology foundation models exist and how they bridge
language and biology, with input representation as the unit of analysis.

**Methods.** PRISMA-ScR scoping review with a PRISMA-S search of eight sources (PubMed, Scopus,
Springer Nature, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, Google Scholar; OpenAlex added in the last
round). Five search rounds covered 2018-01-01 to 2026-08-09. Title/abstract and targeted full-text
section screening used frozen, role-separated LLM pipelines with adjudication and a documented manual
resolution layer. Each model's inputs were charted as grounded routes, one source object carried to
the carrier the model consumes, and classified with a frozen five-family taxonomy. [PENDING: input
paths were further decomposed into reusable data operations for all included papers.]

**Results.** Of 8,170 records identified, 4,862 were screened, 233 full-text reports were assessed,
and 55 records (54 studies) were included, describing 109 models and 585 grounded input routes. No
eligible record was published before 2023 (2023: 4; 2024: 8; 2025: 22; 2026 to August: 21).
Text-native token streams reached 84 of 109 models, dense continuous carriers 39, discrete
biological symbol streams 17, visual raster carriers 11 and geometric/diffusion-state carriers 5.
The most frequent fusion was a shared token sequence (65 models), followed by concatenation (35).
Text acted mostly as an instruction or query (70 models) and carried the biological content itself in
43. [PENDING: operation-level reuse across papers.]

**Conclusions.** [To write after the decomposition results.]

## 1. Introduction

- Large language models are being extended to biological data: single-cell, sequence, imaging,
  spatial and multimodal models [CITE].
- Existing reviews organise these models by architecture, biological domain or task [CITE, see
  `data/existing_reviews_compilation.md`]. They do not compare how biological data become model input,
  although that choice decides what information reaches the model: ranking genes into a sentence,
  projecting an embedding into the token space, or tokenising a sequence directly.
- Gap: no cross-paper, evidence-grounded account of input representations.
- This review: (i) a reproducible living search and screening pipeline; (ii) a route-level taxonomy of
  input carriers; (iii) [PENDING] an operation-level decomposition of each model's input path.

## 2. Methods

### 2.1 Protocol and reporting

Reported following PRISMA-ScR, with PRISMA-S for the search and PRISMA-trAIce-style reporting of
LLM-assisted steps. The protocol (`protocol/PRISMA_protocol.md`, v4.5, 2026-08-09) was not registered.
Amendments are logged in the protocol's amendment section.

### 2.2 Eligibility

Included records describe a generative model with foundation-model characteristics that combines a
text modality (natural language, or gene tokens processed in a generative language-model style) with
at least one biological data modality, published 2018–2026, in English and open access. Exclusions:
no biological modality (EC1), no text component or no substantive text–biology bridge (EC2),
encoder-only or non-generative (EC3), no foundation-model component (EC4), non-computational (EC5),
non-scholarly (EC6), reviews (EC7), duplicates (EC8). Full criteria: `protocol/eligibility_criteria.md`.

### 2.3 Information sources and search

Three concept blocks (biological data AND text/language AND foundation-model/generativity) were
adapted per database (`protocol/queries/`). There was a baseline search (2018-01-01 to 2026-02-28) and
four date-bounded top-ups (to 2026-04-14, 2026-06-10, 2026-07-06 and 2026-08-09). Google Scholar was
rate-limited in the July round and returned no records.

### 2.4 Deduplication and abstract enrichment

Conservative exact matching (DOI, PMID, arXiv ID, normalised title), cross-round matching against
the cumulative master, and a Crossref audit for hidden duplicates. Missing abstracts were enriched from
Semantic Scholar, Crossref and PubMed; records still lacking an abstract were removed before screening.

### 2.5 Screening

Title/abstract screening applied the eligibility decision tree with two role-separated LLM reviewers
(scope and architecture) and an adjudicator for conflicts (Codex CLI, `gpt-5.4-mini`; prompts and
schemas hash-pinned). Full-text screening used Docling conversions; Docling Graph provenance
reconstructed the complete data-source and input-representation sections, which were screened with
the title and abstract. Records still uncertain after adjudication were resolved by the review lead
from the full sections, keeping the automated decision alongside. The roles are prompts executed by
the same model, not independent human reviewers. Run-to-run stability of this screening is reported
in a companion methods paper [CITE companion manuscript].

### 2.6 Data charting: input routes and taxonomy

The unit of charting is a grounded input route: one source object carried through its transformation
chain to the model-visible carrier. Routes were extracted from the full text with three frozen direct
runs plus dense-coverage candidates, and classified by carrier mechanism into five families and 15
subtypes (`input-representation-taxonomy-v1`). Biological modality, lifecycle phase, text role and
fusion topology were charted as orthogonal dimensions. Agreement across the three runs on the 55-record
corpus: route Jaccard 0.945–0.969; carrier-family exact agreement 0.929; Krippendorff's alpha 0.881
(acceptance thresholds 0.80, 0.90, 0.80). Dated author-led amendments are recorded in the atlas metadata.

### 2.7 Operation-level decomposition [PENDING]

Each documented input path is reconstructed as a directed graph of calls to a library of 22 reusable
operations (normalisation, log transform, binning, tokenisation, table lookup, projection,
concatenation, attention and others) with named ports and instance parameters
(`protocol/REPRESENTATION_LIBRARY_GUIDE.md`, library release 1.0.2). Steps whose internal
computation the paper does not state remain unexpanded boundaries. A four-paper pilot (ChatNT,
InstructCell, X-Cell, MUPAD; 47 trajectories, 509 operation calls) was curated by the authors. The
remaining papers are decomposed by an extractor agent and audited by an independent reviewer agent,
with mechanical checks for verbatim evidence, catalog ports, declared parameters and lossless source
restoration (`analysis/operation_decomposition_2026-10-07/README.md`).

### 2.8 Synthesis

Descriptive counts of models per family, subtype, fusion topology, text role and lifecycle phase (a
model is counted once per value it carries), records per publication year, and [PENDING] operation
reuse across papers measured by distinct records per operation.

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Study selection (Figure 1)

The searches identified 8,170 records. After removing 3,083 duplicates and 225 records without a
usable abstract, 4,862 were screened on title and abstract, and 4,599 were excluded. One post-screen
duplicate was removed. Of 262 reports sought, 15 could not be retrieved and 14 lacked a valid targeted
section pair, so 233 reports were assessed. 179 were excluded: no natural-language text component
(131), application wrapper around an existing model (23), not generative (13), review or editorial (5),
no biological modality (3), benchmark or resource without a new model (2), no foundation-model
evidence (1), and no substantive text–biology bridge (1). Fifty-four records were included from the
databases. One more (XunZi) was recovered when the pre-screen lexical validator was corrected and was
screened with the same frozen pipelines, giving 55 records from 54 studies.

### 3.2 Corpus characteristics (Figure 2, Supplementary Table S1)

- The 55 records describe 109 models (29 records describe one model; two describe eight), with
  467 task/input configurations and 585 grounded routes.
- Publication years: 2023 (4), 2024 (8), 2025 (22), 2026 to 9 August (21). None from 2018–2022,
  although the search started in 2018. Years for 13 records added in 2026 top-ups come from the
  date-bounded search window.
- Lifecycle phases charted: fine-tuning (53 models), evaluation (51), pretraining (38), inference (35).

### 3.3 Input-carrier families

- Text-native token streams: 84 models, 325 routes. 46 models use only this family, i.e. biology
  reaches the model as text or as text-like tokens.
- Dense continuous carriers (projected or pooled embeddings): 39 models, 129 routes; most often
  combined with a text stream (18 models).
- Discrete biological symbol streams: 17 models, 56 routes; visual raster carriers: 11 models, 56
  routes; geometric/diffusion-state carriers: 5 models, 19 routes.
- Most frequent subtypes: structured biological prompt or task scaffold (60 models), plain-language
  prompt or question (37), serialised biological context or ordered profile (29), direct projected
  embedding (27).

### 3.4 How text and biology are fused

- Fusion topology: shared token sequence (65 models), concatenation (35), side or generative
  conditioning (17), prefix (14), placeholder replacement (12), shared latent alignment (11),
  encoder–decoder (10), cross-attention (9), retrieval or tool context (5), query bottleneck (4),
  interleaving (2); not determinable for 9.
- Text role: instruction or query (70), biological payload (43), paired alignment supervision (27),
  metadata or context (24), modality or task selector (5), semantic annotation (4), generated output
  (3). Twenty-nine models also have routes with no text.

### 3.5 Operation-level input paths [PENDING]

- parameter realisation (identifier key spaces, table trainability) and where papers leave them
  unstated.

## 4. Discussion (outline)

1. Main finding: most of the field moves biology into the language channel rather than giving the
   language model a new input channel. Tie this to Figure 2b–d.
2. Consequence: the choice of carrier fixes what information survives (ranking or serialisation
   discards magnitudes; projections need connector training). [PENDING operation evidence]
3. Reporting gap: input-path details that papers leave unstated (to quantify with the unexpanded
   boundaries and unrealised parameters from §3.5). Propose a minimal reporting checklist.
4. Field timing: the corpus starts in 2023 and 2026 is on track to exceed 2025, which supports a
   living review.
5. Relation to existing reviews [CITE].

## 5. Limitations

- LLM-assisted screening and charting; stability is reported separately. Role-separated prompts are
  not independent reviewers.
- Open-access and English filters; 15 reports could not be retrieved and 14 had no valid targeted
  section pair.
- Google Scholar was rate-limited in one round; one eligible record was found only after a recall
  correction.
- The withdrawn OKR-Cell preprint is still counted in the 55 records (author decision pending).
- Search closed on 2026-08-09; no refresh was done for this manuscript.
- Protocol objective 3 (datasets, downstream tasks, evaluation metrics) and the extraction fields for
  pretraining objective and code/data availability are not yet charted.
